title: Finally, a Bug Zapper That Actually Zaps (And Does More!)
date: Reviewed in the United States on March 16, 2026
review: Okay, so I've tried a few electric fly swatters over the years, and honestly, most of them have been... fine. They kinda work, sometimes. But this YISSVIC 4000V Bug Zapper Racket? This thing is a total game-changer, and I'm genuinely impressed.Right out of the box, it feels sturdy. Not flimsy plastic like some others. The best part, and what sold me, are the "dual modes." You can use it as a classic handheld swatter, which is great for those ninja-like flies that think they're too fast. And let me tell you, that 4000V really does the trick. You hear a satisfying *POP* and see a little flash, and boom – bug gone. No more chasing them around with a rolled-up magazine only to miss. This is especially good for those annoying mosquitoes that sneak in at night.But the dual mode is where it really shines. It comes with a stand, so you can just set it up on your patio table, kitchen counter, or even next to your bed. It has this soft UV light that attracts bugs, and then *zap*! It's super convenient for those times you just want passive bug protection without having to actively hunt them down. I've been leaving it on my porch during grilling sessions, and it significantly cuts down on the number of flying pests.Charging is easy with a USB cable, and it holds a charge for a good while. There's a safety grid on both sides, so you're not accidentally zapping yourself, which is a nice touch. It's really effective on flies, mosquitoes, gnats, and those tiny fruit flies that love to hang around.Overall, I'm super happy with this YISSVIC zapper. If you're tired of bugs and want something that actually works well and offers more than just the basic handheld option, definitely give this one a shot. It's made my evenings on the patio much more enjoyable. Highly recommend!

title: Watch Out Flies!
date: Reviewed in the United States on February 20, 2026
review: I notices a lot more flies this past summer getting comfortable on my back deck. I bought a dynatrap bug trapper that sits away from social gathering areas, but it does not really attract flies all that much, so I decided I needed a more aggressive, yet fun approach to ridding these flies of my gathering area. Enter the Electric Fly Swatter.Now, an ordinary, warm, summer day should be relaxing. But it is hard to relax with these pesty flies buzzing around you!! So I decided I needed to put in a little work, a little effort before I could truly lay down on the outdoor sectional under the warm rays of that summer sun.I checked the battery level of the Electric Fly Swatter and say it too, was ready for some work.I stealthily opened the slider door to the back deck after noticing the family of flies gather for their afternoon group flight rest. I turned on the Electric Fly Swatter to the top setting (it zaps them itself without you having to hold down the button). I wound up and quickly swatted at the group of about 6 flies. I was able to effectly take out 4, with one stuck in the swatter continuously being zapped until it started smoking. I could have shook the fly out or turned it off, but I felt I had a message to send, so I let it cook. I continued on this mission, eventually going all around my property, eagerly hunting flies. It became a game for me.All in all, this product is light weight, but sturdy. It charges fast and is super effective in his primary duty of fly elimination. Now, it is safe when used appropriately, but it is still safe if you happen to...hit your spouses elbow or knee. Just a quick zap, although probably not recommended. Guess you can teach more than just flies a lesson with this...The sound quality it superb. ZAP ZAP ZAP ZAP!!There is a battery indicator on the front of the handle with three green dots indicating a full charge. On the first setting (just showing the green dots) is the one where you need to press the button on the right side of the handle to use the zapping feature. If you put it on the second setting by sliding the button on the right side up to the top setting, the front of the handle will show a red lightening bolt, indicating that the zapping feature is activated and you do not need to press the size button for it to zap, just go to town!

title: Effective and Convenient Electric Fly Swatter
date: Reviewed in the United States on April 8, 2026
review: The YISSVIC Electric Fly Swatter is an effective tool for dealing with mosquitoes and other flying insects. The 4000V grid quickly eliminates bugs on contact, and the racket-style design makes it easy to target insects directly.The dual modes are useful, allowing it to function as both a handheld swatter and a stationary bug zapper with the purple mosquito light attracting insects. The rechargeable battery is convenient and removes the need for disposable batteries.The build feels lightweight but sturdy, and the handle is comfortable to hold. It’s also easy to use both indoors and outdoors, whether in a home, patio, or while camping. Overall, it’s a practical and efficient solution for controlling flying insects.

title: Surprisingly effective and actually fun to use
date: Reviewed in the United States on May 14, 2026
review: This electric fly swatter works way better than I expected. It charges quickly, holds a good charge, and does an awesome job taking care of flies and mosquitoes. The auto-zap feature is nice, but I mostly use it as a handheld swatter.The best part is the satisfying zap when it hits a fly — sometimes you even get a little smoke effect, which honestly lets you know it’s working. It’s oddly satisfying and very effective.Build quality feels solid, it’s easy to use, and it has definitely helped cut down on bugs around the house. Five out of five for sure.

title: Disappointed but good customer service
date: Reviewed in the United States on November 4, 2025
review: I so wanted to come on here and give a glowing review but after just over two weeks of use I just can’t.For a couple reasons:First, from day one, it was never strong enough to actually kill houseflies without shocking them two or three times, which actually felt inhumane. You get a big show with sparks and lights and a smokey smell, but the fly was just shocked for a moment then would head on its way unless you swatted it again. And again.Luckily, we only had a few of those around. Our big issue has been drain / fruit flies. Which brings me to reason two:After a couple days of valiantly shocking drain flies into non-existence, (same over the top light show, but without the funky smell) half the racket just stopped working. I would put it over one of them as they lounged on a counter top and watch them walk or fly right through the center. If they went towards the top of the racket, sparks flew and no for fruit fly, but anywhere else, nothing. A mere two weeks of use and only half the racket works. Not exactly the best value out there.I’m past the return window by a few days, so I’m stuck with it, luckily it was under $25, so I don’t feel too bad. But if you’re considering, try another product.Update 11/18/25:The seller reached out to me shortly after I posted my review to ask how they could make things right. I unfortunately did not see their email until today, but I really appreciate that level of customer service.I also figured out why the racket was no longer zapping fruit and drain flies. There was a very small piece of lint in between the netting towards one of the outer corners (and when I say small, I’m talking less than 4mm). Once I removed it, the whole racket worked again. It still takes a couple tries to take out a fly, but the little guys are gone no problem.Also, I would like to report the battery life on this is amazing.So I’m upgrading my review to 4 stars.

title: It's OK. I would look elsewhere.
date: Reviewed in the United States on May 14, 2026
review: The rechargeable aspect is nice, and it feels more durable than the executioner. However that is it. It doesn zap many bugs and requires several zaps to even down the bug. It works really well on small bugs because of the tight mesh compared to the executioner. But it barely gets the job done. I wouldn't recommend.One highlight actually is if you have the sun reflect off the electrical surface, that can attract bugs and they will fly into the swatter willingly.

title: Super loud SNAP, Extra power from Lithium battery;  try with flashlight at night!
date: Reviewed in the United States on March 29, 2026
review: I've had 3 different Electric Tennis Rackets before and this one was the best.* Check out the "PRO TIP" at the bottom of this review!!This Racket  has a lithium ion battery instead of regular alkaline cells which generally means higher power.You definitely get a loud "SNAP" and a purple electric flash every time, even for the tiniest gnat.Also, you can just push the switch up to the Auto position and it stays ready to zap.*PRO TIP: if You have lots of trees or bushes etc that your flying  pests hang out in at night, I'd recommend that you turn off as many lights as possible in the yard. Then get a really bright flashlight. Put the electric racket in auto mode. Shine the flashlight through the metal grating of the electric racket, then shake the tree branch or lock the bush with the gnats in it real hard and position the electric racket right next to the tree  or bush with the flashlight shining right through the racket mesh towards the tree.Tonight I was getting 50 to 100 loud "Snaps" per minute as the gnats flew full speed in to the mesh after they got disturbed by the shaking branch and they fly full speed towards the super bright light shining towards them thru the electric racket mesh!Do I know how to have a Good time or what!?!?Also, there was no sign of any electrical weakness at all even after probably 1000 loud snapping kills in maybe 25 minutes.  So yeah, it's a bit pricier than a crappy unit that doesn't even work half the time..But if your looking to handle some flying insects reliably and have a good time doing it, this unit does not disappoint when it's time to handle your business.
